metadata.title: Check Before You Build
metadata.description: Week 3 progress on the AI-Vendor Runway-Risk Scorer: before writing more code, checking whether the recipe already exists, and writing the formal spec with an honest status label. The teach is that verification and honest documentation are engineering, not overhead.

beats.narration_text: Hello Amruta. This week I wrote almost no new scoring code. Instead I did the least glamorous, most important thing in any project: I checked whether the thing I'm building already exists, and I wrote down honestly what state it's in. Boring? Maybe. But skipping this is how people waste a month rebuilding something that was already there. This is week three.

props.command: grep -ril 'runway' recipes/   # does this already exist?
props.runningText: verify it's not a duplicate — then write the spec
output: Check: does a runway recipe already exist in the repo?
Write: the formal recipe spec with typed TODOs
Label it honestly — DRAFT until evidence says otherwise

beats.narration_text: The problem is a trap every builder falls into: you're so excited to build that you never ask whether someone already built it. In a hundred-recipe repository, there's a real chance your idea exists in some form. If you skip the check, best case you duplicate work; worst case you ship a second, slightly-worse version of a thing the team already trusts.

props.command: # excitement to build > checking if it exists
props.runningText: 100 recipes — does yours already live in there?
output: Trap: building before checking what exists
100-recipe repo — your idea might be in there
Skip the check → duplicate or worse, a weaker copy
Cheap insurance: search first, build second

beats.narration_text: So the ask was simple and disciplined: before another line of scoring code, search the whole recipe library for anything doing runway or financial-health work. Not a vague 'I think it's new' — an actual search, with an actual written verdict I can point to if anyone asks. Confirm the gap is real, in writing.

props.topic: THE ASK · SEARCH, THEN WRITE THE VERDICT
props.runningText: search all 100 recipes — write down what you find
output: Search every recipe for runway / financial-health
If it exists → narrow scope or pivot
If not → documented proof the gap is real

beats.narration_text: Here's the verdict I wrote. I searched all hundred recipes. No recipe computes vendor runway as a standalone, sourced, gated artifact. The closest one mentions runway in passing inside a bigger multi-agent brief, but never actually computes it. So the gap is real — and now that's documented, not assumed.

props.title: recipes/OVERLAP_CHECK.md — the written verdict
props.code:
# Overlap check — runway-risk-scorer

Searched all 100 recipes for runway / financial-health work.

Verdict: No recipe computes vendor runway as a standalone,
sourced, gated artifact. The nearest (vendor-intelligence-brief)
lists runway among an agent's concerns but never computes it
as a dedicated metric with a human gate.

Conclusion: the runway-risk-scorer fills a real gap. It is the
only recipe that turns validated funding signals into a
dedicated, fully-sourced runway-risk brief that halts at a gate.

beats.narration_text: With the gap confirmed, I wrote the formal recipe spec. This is the front-matter at the top — the machine-readable header that says what this recipe is and, crucially, what state it's in. Status: DRAFT. Five open to-dos, each one a typed placeholder for work not yet done. This header is a promise about honesty: the label always tells the truth about maturity.

props.title: recipes/runway-risk-scorer.md — the spec header
props.code:
---
recipe: runway-risk-scorer
status: DRAFT              # honest: not yet runnable
recipe_version: 0.1.0
domain: company-intelligence / financial-signals
last_gate: null
todos_open: 5
owner: amruta
---

# Runway-Risk Scorer
#   5 metrics defined · human gate · provenance rule
#   TODO(DEV): trailing-window backfill
#   TODO(DEV): signal-velocity delta
#   TODO(TEST): break tests   ... (typed, not vague)

beats.narration_text: And here's the discipline that ties it together — the lifecycle. A recipe climbs a ladder: draft, specified, runnable-sample, and up. You don't move a rung because you feel ready. You move it because there's evidence in the run log to justify it. This week the recipe earned its first honest label. Every future rung has to be earned the same way.

props.title: the lifecycle — every rung is earned by evidence
props.code:
DRAFT           <- you are here (spec written)
  |  evidence needed: TODOs closed
  v
SPECIFIED
  |  evidence needed: full sample run logged
  v
RUNNABLE-SAMPLE
  |  evidence needed: live data + independent check
  v
RUNNABLE-LIVE  ->  VERIFIED

# the status label is a claim. a claim needs evidence.
# no rung is skipped, none is 'felt' — all are earned.

beats.narration_text: So what does the boring week teach? That checking and documenting aren't overhead — they're the engineering. A searched, written verdict means you're not duplicating work. An honest status label means nobody — including future you — mistakes a draft for a finished tool. The unglamorous week is what makes the glamorous weeks trustworthy.

artifactLines: Search first: confirm your idea isn't already built — in writing.
Spec it: a machine-readable header that states what the recipe is.
Label honestly: DRAFT means draft — don't dress it up.
Earn each rung: status moves on evidence, never on feeling.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Before your next project, spend twenty minutes on the boring part. Search whatever repo or system you're adding to — does your idea already exist? Write one honest sentence about what state your work is really in. Not the state you wish it were. The state it's in. That sentence will save you from lying to yourself later.

props.command: # before building: search + write an honest status
props.runningText: does it already exist? what state is mine really in?
output: 1. Search the system you're adding to — does it exist?
2. Write one honest sentence about your real status
3. Not the status you wish — the status you have
4. Honest labels stop you lying to future-you

beats.narration_text: Check before you build. The boring week is the one that keeps the rest honest. Next week: I try to break my own tool. Hello Amruta.
